meaning: Internal force per unit area inside a material: stress = force ÷ area.
note: Measured in pascals (N/m²), usually MPa for concrete and steel.
hook: Stress is what the material feels; strain is how much it stretches.

meaning: How much a member deforms compared with its original size: strain = change in length ÷ original length.
note: A ratio, so it has no unit.

meaning: A force that makes one part of a material slide past the part next to it.
note: In beams, shear is highest near the supports.
hook: Think of shears (scissors): two blades sliding past each other.

meaning: The turning or bending effect of a force: force × perpendicular distance to the point.
note: A simply supported beam under a uniform load has its largest moment at midspan.
hook: A wrench: longer handle, same push, more turning.

meaning: Twisting of a member about its own long axis.
Sudden sideways bowing of a slender member under compression, before the material itself crushes.
note: Longer and thinner members buckle at lower loads.
hook: Push a plastic ruler end to end — it bows out sideways.

meaning: Slow, permanent deformation of a material under a load that stays on for a long time.
note: Important in concrete: beams and slabs keep sagging slightly for years.
hook: Creep creeps — slowly, over time, under constant load.

meaning: How far a beam or slab moves out of place (sags) under load.
The stress at which a material stops springing back and begins to deform permanently.
note: Reinforcing bar grades are named by their yield strength.
hook: Yield = give in. Past this point it will not return to shape.

meaning: The largest stress a material can take and still return fully to its original shape when unloaded.
hook: Like a rubber band: inside the limit it snaps back.

meaning: A pulling force that tries to stretch a member.
note: Concrete is weak in tension, which is why steel bars are added.

meaning: A pushing force that tries to shorten or crush a member.
note: Concrete and masonry are strong in compression.

meaning: The widened base under a column or wall that spreads its load over enough soil to carry it.
hook: The building's foot: a wider foot sinks less.

meaning: A high-strength steel strand, wire, or bar that is tensioned in prestressed concrete.
hook: Like a body's tendon: it pulls to hold things together.

meaning: A sideways (horizontal) load on a structure, mainly from wind and earthquakes.
